stories.headline: CM Samrat Choudhary directs officials to submit detailed report on flood damage in Bihar
stories.title: CM Samrat Choudhary directs officials to submit detailed report on flood damage in Bihar
stories.summary: He instructed that the Disaster Management Department must obtain assessments of flood damage and rehabilitation costs from all relevant departments and submit a report at the earliest.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) directed officials concerned to immediately submit a detailed report of damages due to flood in Bihar.

He issued the direction during a review meeting in which Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) National President Nitin Nabin and both Deputy Chief Ministers of Bihar Vijay Kumar Choudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav were present along with other officials.
Mr. Choudhary said that a severe flood situation arose this year due to an unprecedented volume of water flowing into the Ganga, Gandak, and Son rivers compared to previous years.
He pointed out that the accumulation of silt in riverbeds is a primary reason for river flooding.
He added that Bihar is the first State in the country to have formulated a silt policy.
The Chief Minister directed that the current status of rivers and the damage caused by floods be continuously monitored.

“A detailed preliminary report on the flood damage should be submitted immediately so that relief, rehabilitation, and necessary development works in the affected areas can be expedited, “Mr. Choudhary said.
He also instructed the DMD to obtain assessments of the flood damage and the costs required for restoration from all concerned departments and submit a report at the earliest.
Mr. Choudhary also directed that necessary arrangements be ensured to address potential issues arising after the drainage of water from the flood-affected areas.
He mentioned that in the second phase, compensation amounts would be transferred to the flood-affected families on October 12, 2026.
Chandrashekhar Singh, Secretary of the Water Resources Department (WRD), briefed about the causes and situation arising from the two phases of flooding in Bihar.
He explained that during the first phase, new peak water levels were recorded in the Ganga, Son, Ghaghara, Kosi, and Punpun rivers, surpassing previous highs.

stories.headline: Congress steps up agitation for removal of Chief Election Commissioner
stories.title: Congress steps up agitation for removal of Chief Election Commissioner
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Transport and BC Welfare Minister Ponnam Prabhakar on Tuesday warned that the Congress would not remain silent if eligible voters were denied their fundamental right to vote, even as Telangana Youth Congress cadres staged a protest outside the State Chief Electoral Officer’s office here demanding the removal and arrest of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Speaking to the media at Sriramulapalli in Koheda mandal of Siddipet district, Mr. Prabhakar alleged that votes of poor and eligible people in rural areas were being removed in the name of revision of electoral rolls.
He accused the Election Commission of India (ECI) failing to function independently and alleged that it was acting under the influence of the Centre.

He condemned the detention of Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi during their protest in Delhi against alleged irregularities in the electoral process, describing the action as undemocratic.
He said the Congress would intensify its ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ campaign from the village level to protect the voting rights of every citizen.
Meanwhile, Telangana Youth Congress president Jakkidi Shiva Charan Reddy led the protest outside the Telangana CEO’s office and demanded his immediate arrest.
Mr. Reddy alleged that the CEC was acting in the interests of the BJP and RSS and claimed that nearly 14 crore votes had been removed across the country without due procedure.
He said the Youth Congress would organise protests across Telangana seeking the resignation of Mr. Kumar.
He warned that the agitation would be intensified if the Centre failed to respond to their demands.
Separately, leaders of INDIA bloc parties staged a protest outside the Hyderabad Collectorate demanding the removal and arrest of Mr. Kumar.
They submitted a representation to the Joint Collector and said their agitation would continue until the CEC was removed and a thorough investigation ordered.

Meanwhile, Congress Khairatabad district president M. Rohit, Secunderabad district president Deepak Jain, MLC Kodandaram, CPI State leader Narasimha, CPI(M) city secretary Venkatesh, Telangana Jana Samithi (TJS) leaders Salim Pasha and Arun Kumar, Hyderabad district president Narsaiah and representatives of the VCK participated in the protest.

stories.title: Supreme Court voids Tamil Nadu's acquisition of temple land
stories.summary: Supreme Court voids Tamil Nadu's acquisition of temple land

article_sentences: The Supreme Court voided a temporary trustee's gift of temple land to the Tamil Nadu government.
The ruling affirmed that custodians must protect temple assets for the deity and worshippers.
The Supreme Court has ruled that a state government cannot legally accept temple property gifted by a temporary trustee, news agency Press Trust of India reported.

A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said the state, as a custodian, cannot unilaterally take over or allow its officers to take over property belonging to religious or charitable institutions that it is required to protect.
The ruling came in a case concerning the ownership of land belonging to the Nagapalayam Mariamman-Ponnachiamman Temple in Tamil Nadu.
The one-acre-and-10-cent plot, comprising Survey Nos. 36/4, 36/5 and 41/2 in Kodumudi village of Erode district, belonged to the temple and was administered by its trust.
On August 30, 2017, the tehsildar issued a certificate stating that S Bhoopathy, the temple's temporary trustee, had given the land to the government.
Through a gift deed executed on the same day, the trustee transferred the land to the Tamil Nadu government, represented by the district collector and the tehsildar.
The tehsildar accepted it for the construction of a taluk office.

M Periyasamy and three others challenged the gift deed, arguing that the transfer of trust property violated Section 34 of the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1959, and was therefore void and illegal.
According to PTI, the Supreme Court said the state had a legal obligation to act as the custodian of the land.

stories.summary: The move consolidates the Dubai-based lender’s Indian operations with RBL Bank after its over ₹26,000-crore acquisition of a 60% stake, as the private lender plans to expand branches and deepen its corporate and wealth businesses.

The approval brings Emirates NBD’s three Indian branches under RBL Bank, following the completion of an over ₹26,000 crore transaction that made the foreign lender the promoter of RBL Bank.

“RBI sanctioned the Scheme of Amalgamation of Indian branches of Emirates NBD Bank P.J.S.C. (Transferor Bank) with RBL Bank Limited (Transferee Bank),” the central bank said in a release, adding that all Indian branches of Emirates NBD will function as branches of RBL Bank from 1 December 2026.
The merger takes effect on 1 December 2026.
From that date, all Indian branches of Emirates NBD will function as RBL Bank branches.
Emirates NBD’s three Indian branches—in Mumbai, Gurugram and Chennai—will become part of RBL Bank.

stories.headline: Supreme Court asks Bengal to allow MP Mahua Moitra to avail circuit house accommodation on a day’s notice
stories.title: Supreme Court asks Bengal to allow MP Mahua Moitra to avail circuit house accommodation on a day’s notice
stories.summary: The MAITC MP had approached the top court seeking guidelines to ensure cooperation from local authorities and the police during visits to her constituency
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (October 16, 2026) asked the West Bengal government to provide Mamata.

All India Trinamool Congress (MAITC) MP Mahua Moitra accommodation at the government circuit house in Krishnanagar, her Lok Sabha constituency, on a day’s notice, instead of requiring three to four days’ advance intimation stipulated by the district administration.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said that Ms. Moitra should be provided accommodation in accordance with the protocol and standard operating procedure (SOP) followed by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-ruled State, while asking her to intimate the authorities a day before her scheduled visit to the constituency.

The Bench also flagged that disputes of this nature ought not to require the top court’s intervention through a petition under Article 32 of the Constitution, which provides a remedy for the enforcement of fundamental rights.
“All that is required is a standard operating procedure (SOP), outlining an advance notice and a nodal officer to whom some personal assistant of the MP can reach out...
If mutual decency and decorum is followed, then these things wouldn’t have come here,” the Bench said.
The court suggested putting in place a protocol governing visits by MPs to their constituencies, particularly in view of the upcoming festive season.

Ms. Moitra had approached the top court seeking guidelines to ensure cooperation from local authorities and the police during visits to her constituency and while undertaking development work under the Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS).
Her petition cited a series of incidents which, she alleged, had impeded her ability to discharge her duties as an elected representative.
Among them was an incident on the night of August 14, when she was allegedly asked to vacate the Nadia Circuit House even as a large crowd gathered outside the premises, abusing and threatening her.
The petition alleged that her requests for police assistance went unanswered.

The incident was followed by a September 1 communication from the Nadia district administration requiring MPs and MLAs to give at least three to four days’ advance notice to avail themselves of accommodation in government guest houses.

stories.headline: Cabinet clears apex body to handle roads, rail, ports as one network
stories.title: Cabinet clears apex body to handle roads, rail, ports as one network
stories.summary: The ITLA will prepare a long-term Transport Plan covering roads, railways, ports, civil aviation and urban mobility, and evaluate government infrastructure projects worth ₹500 crore or more
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) approved a Special Purpose Vehicle — the Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA) — which will be the apex body to plan, appraise and monitor transport and logistics projects that are now handled separately by different ministries and agencies.
Its central task will be a National Transport Master Plan with a horizon of 10 years or more, covering every major mode.

Short-term sectoral plans of about five years, and the annual plans of the transport ministries, will be checked against that master plan so that new capacity is multi-modal rather than mode by mode, according to a statement.
ITLA will also technically appraise Government of India infrastructure projects costing ₹500 crore or more.
Financial appraisal will stay with the existing mechanisms.

The same threshold applies after sanction: the authority will monitor implementation of transport and infrastructure projects above ₹500 crore, run a coordinated mechanism for resolving bottlenecks, and carry out impact assessments once projects are completed.
ITLA will build a National Transport Data Repository, drawing on GSTN e-way bills, FASTag, Vahan, GPS-based systems, and other databases.

ITLA will also technically appraise Government of India infrastructure projects costing ₹500 crore or more.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Stays Demolition Of CSI Church Built As Community Hall In Tamil Nadu's Tenkasi District
stories.title: Supreme Court Stays Demolition Of CSI Church Built As Community Hall In Tamil Nadu's Tenkasi District
stories.summary: The Collector had refused to recognise the community hall as a place of worship citing communal tensions between Hindu and Christian residents.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Collector had refused to recognise the community hall as a place of worship citing communal tensions between Hindu and Christian residents.

The Supreme Court on Friday (October 16) stayed the demolition of a Church of South India (CSI) church in Thippanampatti village in Tamil Nadu's Tenkasi district, in a plea challenging the High Court order finding the structure unauthorised and ordering its restoration as a community hall.
A bench of Justice Vikram Nath, Justice R Mahadevan and Justice Aparesh Singh issued notice on the plea filed by the church trust.
Senior Advocate Huzefa Ahmadi appeared for the church trust.

The case concerns a building constructed by the Tirunelveli Diocesan Trust Association, which was granted permission in 2014 to construct a community hall called the “Church of South India Community Hall”.
The association contends that the building has since been used as a church by the local Christian community, with regular prayers and religious services being conducted peacefully.
The Trust on March 4, 2024, sought recognition of the community hall as a place of worship and permission for the church tower.
However, the District Collector rejected the application on June 25, 2024, refusing permission to convert the community hall into a church and to construct the tower.
The Collector's decision was challenged by the Trust before the Madras High Court.
Before the High Court, the State argued that the original permission covered only a community hall and no approval had been obtained for a spire erected on the building.

Relying on Rule 4(3) of the Tamil Nadu Panchayats Building Rules, 1997, the State submitted that prior approval of the District Collector was mandatory for a site intended to be used for public worship or religious purposes.
The rule permits the Collector to refuse approval if the proposed use is likely to endanger public peace and order.

stories.headline: Delhi Protest | Supreme Court Refuses To Examine Challenge To Section 163 BNSS, Issues Notice On Plea Challenging S. 172 BNSS
stories.title: Delhi Protest | Supreme Court Refuses To Examine Challenge To Section 163 BNSS, Issues Notice On Plea Challenging S. 172 BNSS
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: In the pleas arising from the recent Delhi protests, the Supreme Court on Thursday (October 15) said that it will not examine constitutional validity of Section 163 of BNSS, 2023 (erstwhile Section 144 of CrPC), which empowers executive magistrates to issue prohibitory orders.

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi observed that the Supreme Court had upheld the validity of Section 144 CrPC, the provision corresponding to Section 163 BNSS, in Babulal Parate.
State of Maharashtra, (1961) 3 SCR 423.

The Court, however, notice on a challenge to Section 172 BNSS(which was not there in CrPC), which empowers police officers to detain or remove people who resist, refuse or disregard their directions, and directed the Union Government to file its reply within two weeks.
“Oral submissions were made with regard to the vires of Section 163 BNSS.
However, as the pari materia provision of Section 144 CrPC has been upheld in Babulal Parate.
State of Maharashtra, (1961) 3 SCR 423, we are not inclined to entertain the same.
Accordingly, issue notice, returnable on 19.11.2026, only on the limited issue pertaining to the constitutionality of Section 172 BNSS,” the Court observed.
Section 172(1) BNSS requires people to comply with lawful directions issued by a police officer in the discharge of duties under Chapter XII, which deals with preventive action by the police.

Section 172(2) empowers a police officer to detain or remove anyone who resists, refuses, ignores or disregards such a direction, and either take the person before a Magistrate or release them as soon as possible within 24 hours in petty cases.

The petition argues that the provision allows detention on the basis of a police officer's subjective assessment, without requiring reasonable apprehension of a cognizable offence, recorded reasons or adequate safeguards for judicial scrutiny.
The writ petition seeks a declaration that Section 172 violates Articles 14, 19 and 21, which guarantee equality before law, fundamental freedoms and protection of life and personal liberty.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Grants Bail To Former RG Kar College Principal Sandip Ghosh In CBI Case
stories.title: Supreme Court Grants Bail To Former RG Kar College Principal Sandip Ghosh In CBI Case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on October 15 granted bail to Sandip Ghosh, former RG Kar Medical College Hospital at Kolkata, who was chargesheeted in a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) case involving alleged financial irregularities at the college and manipulation of merit scores to accommodate undeserving candidates.
A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Justice Prasanna B Varale allowed Ghosh's appeal against the Calcutta High Court's February 23, 2026 order rejecting his bail application.

The Court took note of the period of incarceration undergone by Ghosh and the progress of the trial, observing that he had been in custody for more than two years and that only seven out of 147 witnesses had been examined so far.

"In such view of the matter, considering the period of incarceration and also the stage of the trial, we are inclined to set aside the impugned order passed by the High Court and allow this appeal," the Court said.
The Supreme Court accordingly set aside the High Court's order and granted Ghosh bail on such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the concerned trial court.
Ghosh was chargesheeted in Special Case No. 1 of 2025, arising out of a CBI case registered on August 24, 2024, by the agency's Anti-Corruption Branch in Kolkata.

The case involves allegations of criminal conspiracy, criminal breach of trust, cheating, forgery and use of forged documents under Sections 120B, 409, 420, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code, along with offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

The allegations against Ghosh relate to two aspects: financial irregularities at the college where he was the Principal, and the alleged accommodation of undeserving candidates through manipulation of merit scores.
Ghosh had approached the Supreme Court after the Special CBI Court rejected his bail applications on January 7, 2025, followed by the Calcutta High Court's dismissal of his plea on February 23, 2026.
Senior Advocate Siddharth Aggarwal appeared for Ghosh, while Additional Solicitor General Suryaprakash V.Raju appeared for the CBI.

stories.headline: 'If No Concrete Steps Taken, We Will Sit On Dharna' : Supreme Court To Centre On Lack Of Pedestrian Crossing Near Delhi HC
stories.title: 'If No Concrete Steps Taken, We Will Sit On Dharna' : Supreme Court To Centre On Lack Of Pedestrian Crossing Near Delhi HC
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today (October 16) again reiterated its concern over the absence of a pedestrian crossing at the Delhi High Court and orally warned that, if no action is taken at the next hearing, the judges will have to come and stage a dharna (protest) near it until it's done.

A bench comprising Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice KV Viswanathan said this on the lack of basic pedestrian infrastructure at the Mathura Road crossing, which witnesses heavy foot traffic from court visitors and the public.

On September 15, Senior Advocate and amicus Gaurav Agarwal informed the court that the government added a red light, but the bench suggested speed breakers and rumble strips near the Delhi High Court crossing.
Justice Pardiwala had said the matter is very important and had warned that the judges would visit to see if the needful has been done.
Subsequently, on October 5, the Court again directed that a pedestrian crossing be installed at the Delhi High Court and the National Zoological Garden on Mathura Road on a priority basis.

Today, when the matter was taken up, Additional Solicitor General Vikramjit Banerjee submitted that the issue is before a High-Level Committee set up by the Centre to examine what needs to be done at the crossing.
To this, Justice Pardiwala orally stated that the Committee may be fine, but concrete action needs to be taken, or the bench will be constrained to direct the Chief Secretary's presence.
The bench orally warned that if no action is taken by November 25, the judges will go and sit outside the Delhi High Court in tow with ASG until the issue is resolved.
Justice Pardiwala further suggested that the Committee may include the amicus in one of the meetings.
In today's hearing, two contempt petitions were also listed for non-compliance with two previous orders of the Court.

Amicus Agarwal submitted that on April 28, 2025, a bench comprising Justice Abhay S Oka and Justice Ujjal Bhuyan had stated the Union Government had notified Section 164A(scheme for interim relief to claimants) of the Motor Vehicles Act on April 1, 2022 but such an important provision is yet to be notified for more than 3 years.
It remarked that the failure needs to be deprecated and directed them to notify it within 4 months.

stories.headline: India Cements acquires 3.6% stake in Zenataris Renewable for captive power needs
stories.title: India Cements acquires 3.6% stake in Zenataris Renewable for captive power needs
stories.summary: The consideration involved is an equity investment of over Rs ₹20 crore and it will be closed within 120 days from the execution of the agreement
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India Cements on Thursday said that the company has entered into energy supply and share subscription agreement to acquire 3.62 per cent equity shares of Zenataris Renewable Energy Private Ltd, a company engaged in generation and transmission of renewable energy.

“The acquisition is for the purposes of meeting India Cements’ green energy needs, optimising energy cost and comply with regulatory requirements for captive power consumption under electricity laws,” the company said in a filing to the exchanges.
The consideration involved is an equity investment of over ₹20 crore and it will be closed within 120 days from the execution of the agreement.

Zenataris is based in Hyderabad, and is a special purpose vehicle (SPV) established for the development and operation of Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) hybrid renewable energy project located at Kudligi, Vijayanagara District, Karnataka.
The SPV shall supply 11 MW renewable energy to the cement plants of India Cements on a group captive basis, a statement filed by India Cements to the exchanges said.

stories.headline: India's $100 billion China trade deficit: Are non-tariff barriers blocking Indian exports?
stories.title: India's $100 billion China trade deficit: Are non-tariff barriers blocking Indian exports?
stories.summary: Speaking at an interaction in Bangkok, Sitharaman said China's restrictions were preventing Indian products from realising their potential in one of the world's largest markets.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: “With China, I think our trade balance is against us, and it is growing exponentially,” Sitharaman said.
She added that China “uses non-tariff barriers unhesitatingly” and that this was “the biggest hurdle in the in the trade between India and China.”
Sitharaman pointed to phytosanitary regulations, which are intended to prevent the spread of plant pests and diseases, as one of the barriers affecting Indian exporters.
She said Indian products, including generic medicines, beef and vegetables, had “immense” potential in the Chinese market but faced restrictions.
Non-tariff barriers can include licensing requirements, product standards, testing procedures and sanitary or phytosanitary measures.

While such regulations can serve legitimate health and safety objectives, differences in implementation and market-access requirements can increase compliance costs and make it harder for exporters to enter foreign markets.
For Indian businesses, improving access to China could create opportunities across pharmaceuticals and agricultural products.

However, the extent to which these barriers account for the trade deficit would need to be assessed alongside other factors, including the competitiveness of Indian products and the composition of bilateral trade.
Sitharaman said India had refrained from imposing retaliatory non-tariff restrictions or countervailing duties on Chinese goods, despite the widening imbalance.

The finance minister's remarks come as New Delhi and Beijing seek to stabilise relations following the border confrontation in 2020, which triggered prolonged diplomatic tensions and restrictions on Chinese investments and business activities.
Both countries have since taken steps to ease tensions and resume high-level engagement.
However, trade remains a contentious area, with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar also recently saying India was not “getting a level playing field in China.”

stories.headline: India on track to leapfrog Japan in global GDP rankings: Report
stories.title: India on track to leapfrog Japan in global GDP rankings: Report
stories.summary: According to an analysis by The Star, the IMF report underscored the diverging economic trajectories of Asia's two largest democracies.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: According to an analysis by The Star, the IMF report underscored the diverging economic trajectories of Asia's two largest democracies.
New Delhi: India is poised to become the world's fourth-largest economy in 2027, overtaking Japan in nominal GDP terms, a report has said.
The report's forecasts indicate that Japan is expected to retain the fourth position this year but India is projected to move ahead by 2027 with an economy valued at about $4.5 trillion.
The shift would push Japan down to sixth place, behind both India and the United Kingdom, it said.
The projected change comes as India continues to post robust economic growth despite an uncertain global backdrop.
Moreover, the highlighted growth forecast for India in 2026 to 7 per cent, highlighting the country's resilience amid geopolitical tensions and external economic shocks.

Earlier in October, speaking during the release of the IMF's Asia-Pacific regional economic outlook, a senior IMF official said India entered the recent surge in global energy prices from a position of strength, supported by solid growth, fiscal discipline and substantial foreign exchange reserves.
According to the IMF, these strong macroeconomic fundamentals have enabled India to navigate the impact of higher energy costs more effectively than many other economies.
Meanwhile, Japan continues to grapple with a range of structural challenges, including an ageing population, weak domestic demand and sluggish long-term growth.
The IMF has expected that Japan's economy to expand by only 0.7 per cent in 2026.
Higher energy costs and broader inflationary pressures have also weighed on the Japanese economy.
The country has witnessed sustained increases in consumer prices since 2022 with recent geopolitical developments adding to inflationary pressures through elevated fuel and energy costs.
